title: Mastering 6-Digit Code Inputs
summary: This lesson covers essential UX patterns for multi-box authentication codes, including auto-advance, pasting logic, and mobile autofill. It emphasizes providing instant feedback and preventing user errors through smart state management and throttled resend actions.

transcript.text: Paste a six-digit code. Watch the boxes fill themselves.
Most inputs choke on a pasted code. Strip the spaces, drop one digit per box. One paste, six boxes, done.
Type a digit, jump to the next box. Hit backspace on empty, jump back. Your hands never leave the keys.
It looks like six inputs. It is one value split across six slots. Track one string, not six states.
On mobile, force the number pad with inputmode. Then let the phone autofill the texted code. The user taps nothing.
No code arrives, offer resend. But lock it behind a 30-second timer. Otherwise, people hammer it and rate-limit themselves.
Wrong code shakes, clears, and refocuses box one. Right code locks every box in green. Feedback is instant, never a silent fail.
Follow for more UI systems. Save this for your next auth flow.
